item.title: The next little buzz: why BeeGoods exists
item.description: BeeGoods is the goods-focused next chapter beside Med Bee Tate. Here is what we are building, and what we want to get right.

item.title: A honey jar should tell you its story
item.description: A useful buying checklist starts with origin, the product description and the maker—not a beautiful label alone.

item.title: Make your own honey tasting notes
item.description: A simple way to remember what you enjoy without turning breakfast into a competition.

item.title: Before you give honey as a gift
item.description: Think about the recipient, the occasion and the information that should travel with the jar.

item.title: Know what is in a wax product
item.description: A material name is the beginning of a product description, not the whole explanation.

item.title: Choose a candle for the room it will live in
item.description: Shape, scale, scent preferences and product instructions all belong in the decision.

item.title: What we want to know about a handmade soap
item.description: Useful product information helps a maker’s work speak for itself.

item.title: A small gift can carry a good story
item.description: Choose a reason for the gift before choosing more things to put in the box.

item.title: Useful textiles, quieter everyday moments
item.description: Start with what an object needs to do, then decide whether its material and design suit the task.

item.title: A good maker story starts with specifics
item.description: Show the work, name the material and make the next step clear.

item.title: From a market stall to a useful product page
item.description: Bring the clarity of a good in-person introduction onto the screen.

item.title: BeeGoods and Med Bee Tate: connected, with different jobs

item.title: Introducing your goods: a maker’s checklist

item.description: A beautiful launch page is only one part of becoming ready to sell.
